container: Animal testing remains one of the most difficult ethical questions in science. Supporters argue that regulated studies have helped researchers understand disease and develop medicines that save human and animal lives. Critics respond that animals can suffer, cannot consent, and may not reliably predict human responses. Ethical research should therefore follow the principles of replacement, reduction, and refinement. Scientists should use non animal methods whenever possible, limit the number of animals involved, and minimize pain through humane care. Society must weigh potential benefits against suffering, demand transparency, and invest in alternatives that make testing unnecessary.
